ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a rough inclined plane placed on horizontal ground; the inclined plane slopes from the upper left to the lower right; a small block is located on the inclined plane; the arrow F points toward the lower right along the direction of the inclined plane, indicating that the pulling force acts on the block down along the inclined plane. Reasoning: Analyze the forces on the block along the direction of the inclined plane. Originally, the block is still at rest under the action of the pulling force F; the component of gravity down along the inclined plane is mg sinθ, and the pulling force F is also down along the inclined plane, so the static friction force must be up along the inclined plane, with magnitude mg sinθ+F. This shows that the maximum static friction force that this contact surface can provide is at least not less than mg sinθ+F. After the pulling force F is removed, if the block remains at rest, only a static friction force up along the inclined plane is needed to balance the gravitational component mg sinθ; the required static friction force mg sinθ is less than the mg sinθ+F that could already be provided originally. Therefore, the static friction force is sufficient to prevent the block from sliding down, and the block can still remain at rest.
